set.note: 'Kith' comes from an Old English word for acquaintance, kinship or one's native land and survives almost only in this phrase; 'kin' means relatives.

why: Original note said kith 'originally meant friends and neighbors'; Old English cyth(th) primarily meant knowledge/acquaintance, kinship, native land (etymonline); phrase first meant 'country and kinsfolk'
